The final answer of 42 is correct.

A regular hexagon split into six equilateral triangles by its three long diagonals (all meeting at the center) has side length equal to the radius, which equals each triangle's side length. Each triangle has perimeter 21, so its side is 21 ÷ 3 = 7 inches. The hexagon's six sides each measure 7 inches, giving a perimeter of 6 × 7 = 42 inches.

The reasoning is sound. The one claim that needs justification, that each side of the hexagon equals a side of the triangle, holds because the triangles are formed from the center to the vertices, so each triangle has two radii and one hexagon side as its edges.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
